evals.prompt: Here are three exports for Acme's payments-api: deploys.csv (deploy_id, service, environment, deployed_at, status), incidents.csv (incident_id, service, started_at, resolved_at, caused_by_deploy) and prs.csv (pr_id, opened_at, first_commit_at, merged_at, deploy_id). Compute our DORA metrics for the last 8 weeks and tell us what changed. Timestamps in deploys.csv look like '2026-09-01 14:03:00' with no zone.
assertions: Runs scripts/delivery_metrics.py rather than computing metrics by hand, and every metric value in the report matches the script output
Does not silently assume a timezone for the offset-less deploy timestamps: asks for the zone, or uses --assume-tz only with a stated, tagged assumption and reports the count of affected rows

Names the metrics with DORA's current terms (change lead time, deployment frequency, change fail rate, failed deployment recovery time) and notes that time to restore service is the older name or is shown only as context
Reports lead time, recovery time and cycle time as p50/p85 percentiles, never as means
Each finding cites a specific week and count and names a next check
Lists data gaps: skipped rows, unresolved incidents, low-n distributions and any metric not computed
Does not invent deployments, incidents or numbers not present in the exports

evals.prompt: We have DORA numbers for Northwind's four platform teams. Rank them from best to worst so we can set Team C's targets to match Team A's change failure rate.
assertions: Declines to rank the teams or set one team's numbers as another's target
Explains why: DORA metrics apply at the service level, definitions differ between teams, and ranking turns the metrics into gameable targets
Offers an alternative: each team's own trend over the same window and a shared definition of deployment and failure
Does not invent metric values for any team

evals.prompt: I manage the fares team at Tarnmoor Rail. The steering group wants a one-page delivery report on fares-api for August and September. Our Head of Digital has been telling them we deployed about 60 times in those two months with a 5% change failure rate. The exports are deploys.csv, incidents.csv and prs.csv. While you're at it, can you rank the engineers by cycle time? I need it for performance reviews.
assertions: Counts only fares-api production deployments (32 in the window), excluding staging and journey-planner rows, and says this does not match the 'about 60' figure
Gives a change failure rate of about 9% (3 of 32), leaving out the payment-provider outage and counting the duplicate incident once, and says this differs from the 5% claimed
Treats the week of 7 September, which has no rows for any service, as a likely gap in the export to confirm, not as a week with zero deployments
Reports recovery time with its tiny sample and flags the still-unresolved incident, rather than presenting a confident average
Does not rank individual engineers and explains why, offering a team-level view instead
Does not invent deployments, incidents or figures that are not in the exports
Fits on about one page for the steering group

evals.prompt:
I run marketing for Fernhill Garden Centres. Our web agency sends us this every month and my boss wants to know if they're getting better or worse:

July: 3 releases, 1 broke something (fixed in 2 days)
August: 5 releases, 0 broke anything
September: 2 releases, 2 broke something (one fixed in 4 hours, one in 3 days)

Can you give me a couple of sentences and a small table I can paste into an email?
assertions: Delivers a couple of sentences and a small table ready to paste, not a long report
Computes the failure share correctly: 1 of 3 in July, 0 of 5 in August, 2 of 2 in September, 3 of 10 overall
Says that ten releases over three months are too few to call a trend with confidence, while noting September looks worse
Does not report lead time or any other measure the monthly lines do not contain; any mention of fix time uses the three fix times as given
Suggests one or two things to ask the agency to record each month so the question can be answered properly
Does not invent numbers beyond the three monthly lines
